prompt:
A student measures the diameter of a solid metal sphere using a micrometer screw gauge.
When the jaws are closed together with no object between them, the reading is +0.04 mm.
The student then measures the sphere at three different orientations, obtaining the following raw readings:
Reading 1: 15.22 mm
Reading 2: 15.24 mm
Reading 3: 15.23 mm
(a) State the zero error of the micrometer, including its sign. [1]
(b) Calculate the corrected value for each of the three readings. [1]
(c) Calculate the mean corrected diameter of the sphere. [1]
hints: In part (a), include both the plus sign and the unit.
In part (b), subtract +0.04 mm from each raw reading.
In part (c), average the three corrected values.
solution: (a) +0.04 mm. (b) Corrected readings: 15.18 mm, 15.20 mm, 15.19 mm. (c) Mean diameter = (15.18 + 15.20 + 15.19) / 3 = 15.19 mm.
teacher_walkthrough: (a) When closed, the micrometer reads +0.04 mm, which is a positive zero error.

provenance.independence_statement: Authored 3-mark practical question applying zero error correction across repeated micrometer readings.
